findings.description: The security group allows inbound TCP 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administrative access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or exploitation attempts against the instance.
The egress rule permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the instance.

The user_data script exports AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY as plain-text static credentials. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances or from the instance metadata service, leaking long-lived AWS credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the legacy unauthenticated IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the web application could be used to retrieve instance credentials.
The instance is launched without root_block_device encryption configured, so the root EBS volume may store data unencrypted at rest.

The instance is deployed into a public subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and an internet gateway default route, giving it a public IP and direct internet exposure rather than placing it behind a load balancer in a private subnet.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true and no KMS key is specified, leaving attached block storage unencrypted at rest.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted EBS volume, so the backup copy of the data is also stored unencrypted and may be shared or restored without key controls.
The VPC flow log bucket has no server-side encryption configuration (no aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration or KMS key), so audit network logs are stored without enforced encryption.
No public access block, ACL restriction, or bucket policy is defined for the flow log bucket, risking public or cross-account exposure of sensitive network telemetry.
The bucket holding audit flow logs has no versioning or MFA-delete protection and sets force_destroy = true, allowing audit records to be deleted or overwritten without trace.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance launched in this subnet to receive a public IP, placing workloads directly on the internet by default.

The VPC's default security group is not explicitly restricted with an aws_default_security_group resource, so it may permit traffic that an explicitly authored group would not (CIS networking control).
